approved_amendments.scope: Stage a read-only validation WCS for existing repository cleanup candidates.
limits: No deletion, movement, rename, archive, or ignore-rule changes.
Do not execute existing cleanup scripts.
Do not inspect secret contents or alter runtime files.
Any cleanup requires a later, itemized authority.

execution.objective: Refresh and validate the existing repository cleanup candidate evidence against the current repository state, then produce an evidence-backed classification and recommendations without changing repository contents.
success_criteria: Reassess the July 2026 REP-STEWARD-009 and EOS-REPO-001A findings against the actual audit-time checkout; do not treat their classifications as current facts.
Inventory tracked, untracked, and ignored paths separately, recording metadata only for ignored and secret-related paths.

For each existing cleanup candidate, record current existence, Git tracking/status, relevant history or references, evidence source, confidence, and disposition: PROTECTED, ACTIVE, REVIEW, MISSING, or UNKNOWN.
Statically inspect the existing stage-two candidate and execution scripts; record their broad filename-pattern and recursive-deletion behavior without executing them.
Exclude .git internals, do not follow paths outside the repository root, and do not read secret values.
Produce a human-readable report and machine-readable candidate register under execution/workspace/REP-STEWARD-018/ only after a separate implementation authority is approved.
Make clear that a candidate classification or recommendation does not authorize deletion or movement.
No files are deleted, moved, renamed, archived, or edited during this validation cycle.

depends_on: EOS-REPO-001A cleanup candidate artifacts under GP-EXEC-010M-06A
unlocks: A separately reviewed, itemized cleanup WCS if the validation report supports cleanup.

verified: REP-STEWARD-009 records discovery complete and cleanup not started, with Dead Artifact Validation as the first recommended authority.
REP-STEWARD-014 through REP-STEWARD-017 concern authority registries, registry integrity, relationships, and adoption readiness.
The inspected EOS-REPO-001A execution script recursively removes broad classes of backup/candidate files and selected recovery directories.
not_yet_evidenced: Whether the July 2026 candidate list matches current repository contents.
Whether each candidate is referenced by current authority, build, runtime, recovery, or audit workflows.
The current counts and disposition of tracked, untracked, and ignored candidate paths.

forbidden_surface: All deletion, move, rename, archive, or cleanup execution

validation_cases: A tracked backup or pre-mutation file is not classified as dead solely because of its name.
A missing historical candidate is reported as missing, not deleted or silently discarded.
Secret files are counted or classified by path metadata only; their contents are never read.
The existing recursive cleanup script is reviewed statically and never invoked.
Candidates with uncertain ownership, references, or recovery value remain UNKNOWN or REVIEW.
The validation report makes no cleanup recommendation without evidence and per-item disposition.

founder_runtime_test.test_definition: No application runtime change is authorized.
founder_runtime_test.expected_outcome: A reviewed, evidence-backed candidate assessment with no repository cleanup performed.
